'''Harry Erwin Nursten''' (August 1927 – 20 December 2011) was a British [[Food chemistry|food chemist]], specialising in [[Flavor (taste)|flavour]] chemistry at the Department of Nutrition and Food Sciences at the [[University of Reading]].

==Biography==
Harry Erwin Nursten was born in Czechoslovakia in August 1927, son of Sergius Nursten and Helene. The family managed to escape to England shortly before the [[Second World War]]. In the 1939 England and Wales Register<ref>Ancestry.co.uk</ref> the parents (“Nursem”) were living at Corringham Court, Golders Green;  Sergius was listed as “Dental surgeon (seeking work).” The family settled in [[Ilkley]], Yorkshire, where Harry attended [[Ilkley Grammar School]] and gained his [[Higher School Certificate (England and Wales)|Higher School Certificate]] in 1944.<ref>{{cite news|title=Higher School Certificates|newspaper=Yorkshire Post and Leeds Intelligencer|page=3|date=25 August 1944}}</ref> He went to the [[University of Leeds]] where he read colour chemistry and dyeing, followed by a PhD in colour chemistry, awarded in 1949.

In the summer of that year Nursten was one of a group of volunteers harvesting at [[Windlestone Hall]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Colling|first=Keith|title=Living in a mansion on a harvest holiday|newspaper=Yorkshire Post and Leeds Intelligencer|date=15 August 1949}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Colling|first=Keith|title=Harvest volunteers thanked with peaches and cream|newspaper=Yorkshire Post and Leeds Intelligencer|date=22 August 1949}}</ref> Also there was Jean Frobisher, Harry's fellow student and bridge partner at Ilkley Grammar School, and now a welfare worker. They were married on 23 December 1950 at St Paul's Church, [[Esholt]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Marriages|newspaper=Yorkshire Post and Leeds Intelligencer|date=27 December 1950}}</ref>

After more research at Leeds, Nursten taught dyeing and textile chemistry at [[Nottingham Trent University|Nottingham Technical College]]. He returned to Leeds in 1955 as a lecturer in the Procter Department of Leather Science.<ref>{{cite web|title=Food and Leather Science, Procter Department of|website=University of Leeds Archives: Special Collections|url=https://explore.library.leeds.ac.uk/special-collections-explore/4137|access-date=23 May 2020}}</ref>

Following two sabbaticals at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and [[UC Davis]], he moved into the area of food and flavour science. In 1976, he was appointed Chair of Food Science at the [[University of Reading]]. Following the merger of the National College of Food Technology and the Department of Food Science, he became Head of Department of one of the biggest [[Food Science]] Departments in the UK. In 1992, the year he retired,<ref>{{cite web|title=Tribute to Harry Nursten|website=SCI|url= https://www.soci.org/news/thames-kennet/thames-kennet-nursten}}</ref> Nursten ensured that the [[Hugh Macdonald Sinclair]] [[Financial endowment|endowment]] was used to set up a new centre for human [[nutrition]] research at the [[University of Reading]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reading.ac.uk/internal/staffportal/news/articles/spsn-426950.aspx |title=Professor Harry Nursten 1927 – 2011 |access-date=2018-09-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918160546/https://www.reading.ac.uk/internal/staffportal/news/articles/spsn-426950.aspx |archive-date=2018-09-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Harry Nursten died in Reading on 20 December 2011. His wife, Jean Patricia Nursten, is a noted Professor of social work,<ref>{{cite web|title=Nurtsen, Jean Patricia (Frobisher)|website=Encyclopedia.com|url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/culture-magazines/nursten-jean-patricia-frobisher|access-date=24 May 2020}}</ref> and author.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean Nursten: Books - Amazon.co.uk|website=Amazon.co.uk|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Books-Jean-Nursten/s?rh=n%3A266239%2Cp_27%3AJean+Nursten|access-date=24 May 2020}}</ref>
